To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the observed and perceived influences of the family environment on problem-focused coping behavior of children with spina bifda (SB) are different and change with age.
the observed and perceived family influence on problem-focused coping of preadolescent children with spina bifda is associated with the children's coping behaviors.

1) the observed family influences of parental involvement, parental support, and family cohesion predicted the problem-focused coping behaviors (coping self-efficacy and problem-focused coping) of preadolescent children with spina bifda; and 2) the perceived family influences of family involvement, parental support and family cohesion predicted perceived problem-focused coping of preadolescence children with spina bfida.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method to measure family influences on problem focused coping behaviors of pre-adolescents with Spina Bifida.
the development of a new generation of high performance computing systems.
the development of a model for the study of the relationship between the family and the development of problem-focused coping skills.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no differences in coping behaviors between preadolescent children with spina bifda and their non-disabled peers.
the study of the relationship between family influences and problem-focused coping behavior of preadolescent with spina bifda is a complex and multifaceted issue.
the study of the family system is an important aspect of the study of the development of coping behaviors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the family influences on coping behaviors of children and adolescents with spina bifda can be best understood by examining family influences on the child's problem-focused coping behavior, family coping behavior, and family coping resources.
the family is the primary context for development and socialization.
we have shown the importance of family functioning and family processes as predictors of children’s coping with stress and that these family variables can be measured in a reliable and valid manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to better understand the impact of family on the coping behaviors of pre-adolescent children with spina bifda.
the family is a key influence on the problem-focused coping of preadolescent children with spina bifda.
we need to think about how we can support families in a way that allows them to be more effective in supporting children's coping and adjustment.
